02 / Color

Let contrast lead.
Let color speak.

Build the page in Jet Black and Studio White. Give an action or a section its own accent. Keep the name monochrome until interaction brings in Sky Blue.

Click a swatch to copy its hex. Use dark text on pastel fills; reserve pale text for dark surfaces.

The Socials exception.

Instagram’s multicolor glow, TikTok’s cyan and pink, and the other platforms’ own colors identify their destinations. They belong on those links; the core identity stays within the six colors above.

03 / Typography & composition

Say it big.
Give it space.

Arial Black / Display

Stories
worth
sharing.

Heavy weight. Tight tracking. Solid letterforms.

Myriad Pro / Body

Real people. Meaningful moments. A thoughtful eye for the details that make a story yours.

Use Myriad Pro when available, with Myriad and Arial as fallbacks. Keep body copy open and easy to read.

Display
Arial Black, Arial, sans-serif · 900 weight
Body
16–18px · generous line spacing
Eyebrows
Small, bold capitals · spaced lettering
Page rhythm
Wide gutters · short paragraphs · one clear next step

The signature divide.

A diagonal moves from black into white. Letter color follows the surface beneath it so the title reads as one continuous statement.

Space does the framing.

Alternate light and dark chapters. Let a small eyebrow introduce a large headline, then a short thought and a clear action.

Room on every screen.

Stack columns on mobile, scale titles to fit, and keep moving letters clear of the edges. Preserve comfortable touch targets.

04 / Shape & surface

Soft glass.
A little glow.

Circles and rounded squares form the background. A quiet tint, a thin light edge, and a soft inner highlight give them depth. Keep their centers clear of important copy.

Simple forms. Layered light.

Light follows your hand.

Buttons carry more color than the background. Their rounded shape, glassy shine, and soft glow make the next step easy to find.

Socials Acting Film Video

Live links, with a pointer-following shine. Pill actions and rounded cards share the same material.

05 / Motion

It has weight.
It finds its way home.

Motion is a response to the person exploring. The title above uses the homepage’s actual spring behavior, and the glass throughout this guide uses its weighted parallax.

01

Touch, then return.

Letters gently repel the cursor, light up blue, and settle back into their original place. The word stays anchored and readable.

02

Depth as you move.

Cursor movement shifts the scene subtly. Glass layers travel at different depths; larger shapes feel slower and heavier.

03

Ease into the scroll.

Background forms follow scrolling with a soft lag, then settle. Content keeps a steady reading order and a clear visual hierarchy.

Keep it comfortable.

Respect reduced-motion preferences. On small screens, use gentler movement and stacked layouts. Links stay usable by touch and keyboard, with a visible focus state.

06 / Voice & imagery

A person.
Not a pitch.

Write like Jet is in the room: direct, curious, and welcoming. Short sentences carry the idea. Real portraits and real work carry the personality.

“Let’s make something.”A warm, specific invitation.
“Tools for the story.”The equipment serves the work.
“Two filmmakers. One shared vision.”A simple idea with a human center.

Use portraits with breathing room. Let photography feel personal, and keep decorative glass behind the subject.

07 / The essentials

Make it feel
like Jet.

Start with the real assets. Keep proportions intact, choose the crop for the space, and let the surrounding layout do the rest.
